messages:
Jamie (eng-runtime): quick sync — after the microbatch size audit, we saw p95 fine but p99 for streaming chat spikes when mb=2 vs mb=8. digging in now.
Liam (perf): can you paste the raw tail numbers?
Jamie (eng-runtime): p95 ~ 80ms both. p99 goes from 420ms (mb=8) -> 920ms (mb=2) on the same GPU profile. throughput drops as expected but tail doubles.
Tasha (runtime): interesting. did the kernel selector change for short sequences? smaller mb tends to favor the "single-token matmul" path which we recently regressed.
Jamie (eng-runtime): repro script: ```bash
# streaming repro (small prompt)
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"stream":true,"prompt":"hi\n"}' https://api.redwood.local/v1/chat --header 'X-MB-SIZE:2'
```
Liam (perf): ran nvprof on that run — stack shows fallback to matmul-generic at hot path for causal-attn with seq_len=8. kernel hint currently picks fp16-warp-k for mb>=4, but for mb<4 it picks generic.
Tasha (runtime): right — selector rule is `if mb < 4 or seq < 16 -> generic`. that was to avoid kernel launch overhead but maybe the generic kernel has worse tail for streaming because it serializes work in a different block size.
Ana (eng-sre): any KV cache behaviour? streaming chat should hit cached past tokens; when mb small we might thrash KV eviction. logs?
Jamie (eng-runtime): KV hit% drops from 98% -> 86% on the small-mb run. looks like more cold-starts per connection. might be because we create more microbatches per session and evict older KV entries between writes.
Liam (perf): profile shows two causes: (1) kernel fallback increases per-token compute time variance, (2) extra KV miss + refill causes occasional 400ms stall. they compound.
Tasha (runtime): reproduce trace (trimmed): ```
TRACE: request=abcd mb=2 seq=48
KV_LOOKUP: hit=true time=2ms
KV_LOOKUP: hit=false time=120ms (refill)
KERNEL: matmul-generic time=240ms
KERNEL: matmul-warp time=18ms
```
Jamie (eng-runtime): so occasional KV miss + generic kernel == tail. the miss triggers more memory traffic and kernel scheduler picks slower path.
Liam (perf): hypothesis: with mb=2 we get more context-switch-like scheduling between connections, spilling KV to LRU. fixing selector + KV pin for recent sessions might help.
Tasha (runtime): quick patch idea: (A) tweak kernel selector to prefer warp-k for mb>=2 when seq >= 16; (B) add a small KV "session pin" TTL (200ms) to avoid eviction between microbatches for active session.
Ana (eng-sre): TTL change is low-risk? could increase memory pressure on overloaded nodes. need a guard: only enable pin when active_mem < 80%.
Jamie (eng-runtime): agreed. let's try a canary config: `selector.pref_hint = "favor-warp-mb2"` and `kv.session_pin_ttl_ms=200` gated by mem. I'll deploy to staging.
deploy-bot: deploy started — canary group: 3 pods (gpu-type: a100-s)
Liam (perf): running the staged workload now. preliminary: p99 dropped from 920ms -> 340ms with both changes. p95 unchanged. KV hit% back to 97.5%.
Tasha (runtime): nice. can we isolate which change contributed more? toggle tests?
Jamie (eng-runtime): ran ablation: selector-only -> p99 480ms; ttl-only -> p99 520ms; both -> 340ms. so both contribute.
Ana (eng-sre): monitoring: memory 72% avg, 78% p95. no OOM. enabling mem guard for production rollout.
Liam (perf): one more optimization: add a microbatch hysteresis so small bursts from a connection avoid flipping selector rapidly. e.g., if session used warp kernel recently, keep it for next N microbatches. reduces variance.
Tasha (runtime): sounds good. will drop a PR with the selector tweak + hysteresis + config flags. also adding metrics: kernel_type, kv_hit, session_pin_active per request for observability.
Jamie (eng-runtime): action items: 1) Tasha PR for selector + hysteresis (link when ready); 2) Ana to flip canary to prod with mem guard; 3) Liam to run longer soak to validate p99 over 24h.
Ana (eng-sre): starting prod rollout tomorrow 10:00 UTC with 10% traffic. will pause on error>=1% or p99 regresses >10% for 5m.
Jamie (eng-runtime): thanks — this also explains why non-streaming completions didn't see the same tail: they batch bigger (mb>=8) so kernel picks warp path and KV warmed per-batch. streaming workloads need the special casing.
Liam (perf): will write a short doc for the kernel selector rules and tradeoffs (latency SLO vs throughput) so product teams know why streaming gets different defaults.
Tasha (runtime): 👍 I'll add unit tests around selector and simulate kv miss patterns.
Jamie (eng-runtime): closing the loop: if anyone sees new tail after rollout ping here with traces. good first step. :rocket:
